headline: Salem State redevelopment breaks ground on 473 rental homes
dek: The former South Campus project will add rental housing in two phases while directing sale proceeds toward Salem State’s North Campus modernization.
body: A redevelopment of Salem State University’s former South Campus officially moved toward construction Friday, with plans for 473 new rental homes on about 23 acres along Harrison Road and Loring Avenue. The [Massachusetts Division of Capital Asset Management and Maintenance announced the groundbreaking](https://www.mass.gov/news/healey-driscoll-administration-celebrates-groundbreaking-for-nearly-500-new-homes-on-salem-state-south-campus), and [Salem Patch independently reported the event](https://new.patch.com/massachusetts/salem/salem-state-south-campus-breaks-ground-473-new-rental-homes).

The project is divided into two phases. Avalon Salem, the first phase, is planned to create 340 rental homes, with construction expected to begin this winter. The state release describes the affordability mix using 80% and 60% of area median income thresholds. Those designations are affordability rules, not a promise that every unit will carry the same rent or serve the same household size.

The second phase, Forest River Residences, is expected to add at least 133 homes. The state says at least 40% of those units will be affordable to households at or below 60% of area median income, and that phase is expected to close in 2028. That timetable describes the planned financing milestone; it is not a guaranteed occupancy date for the homes.

The land is being redeveloped through the Healey-Driscoll administration’s State Land for Homes initiative, which uses surplus or underused public property for housing. The administration says the initiative had advanced plans for more than 5,600 homes during its first year. That is a pipeline figure, meaning homes in different stages of planning and development rather than units already completed or occupied.

For Salem, the project links a housing decision with a campus-consolidation plan. Proceeds from the sale of the South Campus property are expected to support capital investments on Salem State’s North Campus through SSU BOLD, the university’s long-term effort to address infrastructure needs and consolidate the campus footprint. University President John Keenan said the sale allows the public institution to reinvest in teaching and learning facilities while the city gains new housing.

The redevelopment has been moving through a Chapter 40R Smart Growth overlay district. [Historic Salem Inc.](https://historicsalem.org/advocacy/forest-river-residences/) describes the site as an active project and says the overlay sets design standards and a 20% affordability requirement for the district. The preservation group also says it is watching how the plan handles the former St. Chretienne School and Convent buildings and the surrounding neighborhood. Those are planning and preservation concerns that will continue alongside construction; they do not change the housing totals announced for the two phases.

The state’s project description says the South Campus redevelopment is intended to make productive use of land no longer needed for its original institutional purpose. Its local impact will depend on several later steps: the first phase must begin and complete construction, the affordability commitments must be implemented, and the second phase must reach its expected 2028 closing. The university must also translate the property proceeds into the North Campus work described in its modernization plan.

For now, the groundbreaking establishes a concrete schedule for a large North Shore housing project. The next near-term marker is the start of Avalon Salem construction this winter. Later updates will show when applications open, how the income-restricted units are structured, and whether Forest River Residences advances on the financing timeline set out by the state and developer partners.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Salem State South Campus breaks ground on 473 rental homes
seoDescription: A two-phase redevelopment of Salem State’s former South Campus will create 473 rental homes and support North Campus modernization.
